guideWindow.guideWindow.title: DeskPet · Getting Started
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeA: The macOS settings controls will open next. Save each step to continue. If you close the guide, you can resume it later from the menu bar.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeAA: Data is saved in Application Support / DeskPet and retained during app upgrades. You can export history from Full Chat. API keys used on Windows must be entered again on your Mac.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeAC:
Quick Chat and Full Chat share a session. Paste, drag and drop, or use + to add images and files; remove them before sending if needed. Folder attachments reference only the path: they do not read its contents or change permissions. Image input requires a compatible model.

Replies support Markdown. Reasoning and processing time update continuously; the activity details collapse when the reply appears. Reopen them from the reply’s More menu.

On Windows, switch between Chat and Work modes at the bottom left of the input box or with Tab. Use + to attach a recent app window snapshot. macOS currently supports chat only, without the file agent or app snapshots.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeAE:
Work Settings controls file access, default directories, plan mode, ongoing goals, backups, turn limits, and time limits. Changes apply to the next request; saving does not run a task.

The file agent is currently available only on Windows. It can read, search, create, and edit files, create folders, and open directories. Full access uses the current account’s existing file permissions; the working-directory-only setting restricts the scope, and plan mode is read-only. Stopping keeps completed changes. Multiple request turns may use model credits.

Work Settings is visible on macOS, but its controls are currently unavailable.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeAG:
Start at login is enabled only if you turn it on in the General tab. Use About to check versions and open the download page. On macOS, download and replace the app manually.

Right-click your companion to open the menu. Use the four-slot action wheel for snacks or naps. You can reopen setup from the menu bar later. Finishing setup does not mean skipped services are configured or have passed a connection test.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeC: Ebao includes full default and special outfits and works offline. The other four companions retain their names and avatars. After setup, select one to download their full character pack, or use Download / Update All. During setup, selecting a companion only displays information; it does not switch or download. Switching later stops the previous companion’s ongoing conversation.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeD: Size, Always on Top, and Position
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeE: Adjust size and always-on-top behavior in General. Drag your companion to move them. Locking their position prevents movement.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeG: Wandering is attempted every 90–180 seconds, with the timer reset after interaction. Mouse tracking, naps, and landing stumbles each have their own switch.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeI: Add providers in the Model Configuration tab. Each provider stores its own URL, API key, and proxy. Presets can be customized. On Mac, API keys use Keychain-backed encryption.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeK: Fetch the model list and select multiple models to add, or enter a model ID and display name manually. Click Save and Enable This Provider / Model to apply.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeM: The persona in the Companion tab is saved separately for the current companion. Click Save Persona after editing. You can restore the original persona at any time.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeO: Double-click your companion or choose Quick Chat from the menu bar. Type a message and click Send / Queue, or press ⌘ + Enter.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeQ: In Full Chat, edit, delete, and reorder queued messages on the right, or use Steer Now. Stop cancels the current request and pauses the queue. Quick Chat and Full Chat share the same session.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeS: Configure a separate recognition service in Dictation. Microphone access is requested only when you click Dictate / Finish Recording in chat. Click again to transcribe into the draft, then review and send.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeU: Configure a separate service in Cloud Read Aloud. In Voice, choose system or cloud read aloud and save a voice for the current companion. Previewing uses the selected service.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeW: Configure Gemini’s native real-time service in Live and save a voice in Voice. Click Live in chat to start. Closing the window releases the audio devices.
guideWindow.steps.steps.alternativeY: In General, turn off read aloud and configure click-through mode and global shortcuts. With click-through enabled, use the menu bar to reopen Settings. Shortcut conflicts show an error.

onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeA:
This guide introduces DeskPet step by step. You do not need to configure everything at once.

"Skip This Step": Skip the current action.
"Skip This Chapter": Skip this chapter and continue to the next.
"Continue Later": Save your progress and resume here next time.
"End Setup": Exit setup; reopen it from Settings later.

These buttons are always available. During setup, choosing a character, starting a download, or clicking a test sends the corresponding network requests. Playing audio or enabling the microphone requires your explicit action.
Hold the left mouse button on an opaque part of your companion’s body, drag a short distance, and release. Actual movement unlocks the next step. Skip if needed.
Try It: Right-Click Menu
Right-click your companion’s body to open the menu, then click outside it to close. This exercise only opens the menu; its actions are temporarily disabled.
Try It: Action Wheel
Middle-click your companion’s body to open the action wheel, then choose an action. The wheel avoids screen edges. Select an action to finish this step.
Try It: Click to Interact
Click your companion’s head or body and wait for a pat or poke animation. A double-click that opens Quick Chat does not count.
Try It: Double-Click for Quick Chat

Quickly double-click your companion’s body with the left mouse button to open Quick Chat. This is a preview: sending and recording are disabled. Close it at the top right. Reopening starts a new empty conversation without the previous context. Open older records from the "Quick Chat" group in Full Chat.
Add text service provider

Click "Add" and select your service provider. You can skip this chapter if you don't have an account; deselecting will not delete the filled-in content. A service provider can save multiple models, but only one can be selected for the current model.
Check text interface address
Expand Connection Settings and check the provider’s base URL. Use the provider’s official API or your own compatible endpoint. Do not enter the web chat URL as the API URL.
Select interface protocol
OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages use different protocols. Choose the protocol required by your provider, rather than relying on the model name.
Fill in the text API Key
Enter this provider’s API key. It is encrypted for the current Windows user. This guide does not display or copy keys. Leave it blank for self-hosted services that allow anonymous access.
Configure text proxies on demand

Enable this only if the service needs a proxy. The default local URL is http://127.0.0.1:7890. Make sure the local proxy is running. This proxy applies only to this service; update download acceleration is separate.
Get a list of available models

Click "Save and Get Model List" in the connection area, or "Get Model List" in the model area. This will query the service without sending the chat content; successful acquisition only proves that the list interface is available, but does not mean that the chat has been verified.
Add models one by one
Click + beside each fetched model to add it individually. In the model dialog, set its display name, capabilities, and context capacity, then save or add. There is no bulk box selection.
Add manually when list is not available
Click "Custom Model" and enter the provider’s full model ID. A failed model-list request does not necessarily mean chat is unavailable. Check account permissions if unsure.
Fill in the model context capacity
onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeB: Choose Companion

Enter the provider’s published context capacity in tokens in the model editor. Keep the detected value if available, or use 0 if unknown; Work Settings supplies the runtime fallback. Set image and tool capabilities according to the actual model.
Check Tool and Image Capabilities

In the model editing window, select automatic/supported/unsupported for tool calling and image understanding. User settings take priority, followed by clear metadata returned by the current service; if neither exists, the old unverified compatibility judgment will be used. Changing the service address will clear out old metadata. Enabling it does not mean that the service will be available, nor will it expand project permissions.
Select the current model in use
Select one of the added models as the current model. Switching models takes effect from the next request; existing drafts will not be automatically sent.
Whether to use streaming replies
When enabled, text appears as it arrives. Some compatible APIs support only non-streaming replies. If replies are empty or a protocol error occurs, turn this off and retry.
Save text configuration
"Save and Continue" saves only the text service page. It does not save unfinished speech recognition, read aloud, or Live settings.
Verify a real text request
Click "Send Text Test" to send a short test without adding it to chat history. It may use a small amount of credit. Only a nonempty reply counts as passing. You can skip the test.
Troubleshoot the Text Connection

401/403: Check Key, account and model permissions; 404: Check interface address, protocol and model ID; Timeout: Check network and proxy. The success of the model list and the success of the real reply are two different verifications. Do not post the key or full service response to others.
Understanding speech recognition
ASR converts your recording into text, then passes it to the text model. It does not read replies aloud and differs from Live real-time voice. Skip this chapter if you only type.
Choose a Speech Recognition Service
Click "Add" to choose a speech recognition provider. The text service’s API key is not reused automatically. Check that your account has speech recognition access.
Check the Speech Recognition URL
Check the speech recognition service URL. The editable model ID must identify a speech recognition model supported by the provider. Prefilled values are only a starting point.
Fill in the recognition model
Enter a speech recognition model ID. This page does not fetch a model list. Do not use an ordinary text chat model.
Enter the Speech Recognition API Key
Use an API key with speech recognition access. Leave blank for an anonymous self-hosted service. The text service’s key is not applied automatically.
Speech Recognition Proxy
Enable the service's own proxy as needed and check the address and port. Recording uploads will go through this connection; only use services you trust.
Save recognition configuration
onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeC: The app includes the complete Ebao character. You can choose a companion during setup. Installed characters can appear immediately. If the selected character’s pack is missing or needs updating, it is prepared in the background while the current usable character stays visible. When preparation finishes, the most recently selected companion is loaded. You can continue the guide in the meantime. Persona and voice preferences are saved separately for each companion.
Saving does not start recording. The microphone is requested and recording starts only when you click it in chat.
Know how to stop, send and cancel recordings

Click the microphone in chat to dictate. Stop leaves the transcription in a draft; Send transcribes and submits; Esc cancels. Check recognized text before sending to avoid passing recognition errors to the model.
Understand the Three Voice Switches

"TTS Output" controls automatic read aloud. "Use Cloud TTS" chooses cloud or Windows system speech synthesis. Live calls use separate audio. Test Read Aloud checks playback without sending a chat message.
Set Automatic Read Aloud

Enable "TTS Output" to read model replies automatically. Turning it off stops current automatic playback. Do Not Disturb pauses automatic read aloud while keeping this preference; its silence does not mean cloud settings failed.
Set volume

First set the volume to a moderate value, and confirm that the current output device in Windows is available and the application is not muted. Sliders are saved instantly. When the volume is 0, no sound is heard even if the interface is successful.
Choose System Read Aloud or Cloud TTS

"Use Cloud TTS" off: Use Windows system voices without a cloud API key.
On: Use the cloud model and voice below. Adding a read aloud model alone does not enable cloud TTS. Turn this switch on to use the cloud.
System Read Aloud
Cloud TTS is off, so the cloud URL, model, and API key steps are skipped. Save and test Windows speech directly. Install missing voices in Windows language and speech settings.
Add a Cloud Read Aloud Service
Cloud TTS is on. Click "Add" to choose a TTS provider and check that your account has text-to-speech access. This service reads text aloud; speech recognition and Live are separate.
Check cloud TTS address
Fill in the API address required by the provider. Do not fill in the web page address, ASR address, or Live's WSS address. If the request fails, check this address first.
Check the TTS Protocol
Choose OpenAI Audio, MiMo Chat Audio, or Auto-Detect as required by the provider. Some models use different audio protocols; similar names do not imply compatible APIs.
Enter the Cloud TTS Model
Enter a speech synthesis model ID your account can call. This page does not fetch a model list. Edit prefilled models according to provider documentation.
Enter the Cloud TTS API Key
Enter this TTS service’s own API key. Working text chat does not prove TTS access. Keys are encrypted locally. Leave blank for anonymous self-hosted endpoints.
Choose or Enter a Voice

Choose from the list or enter the provider’s voice ID. The voice must match the model. Voice preferences are saved per companion, service, and model. Preview recommended voices to confirm they suit you.
Configure the Read Aloud Proxy
onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeD: Remember Where to Find Settings
Enable a separate proxy for read aloud if needed. The text service’s proxy and update acceleration do not replace this connection setting. Leave it off if unnecessary.
Save Read Aloud Settings
Saving records the current engine, cloud service, and voice. It validates configuration format without proving that the service can synthesize speech. The next step offers a playback test.
Try It: Test Read Aloud

Click the highlighted "Test Read Aloud". It uses the saved engine, model, and voice to read a short passage. Cloud services may charge for this. Wait for completion, then confirm in the guide whether you heard audio. If playback is inconvenient, skip this step; it cannot count as verified.
Practice Stopping Read Aloud
Click "Stop Reading Aloud" at any time during the test. This does not change your automatic read aloud preference or stop Live. If you heard nothing, use the next step to troubleshoot.
Check item by item when there is no sound

Check the system output device, app volume, and volume here. Then check whether cloud TTS is on, the API key belongs to the TTS service, and the voice matches the model. For 401/403, check authorization; for 404, the URL and model; for timeouts, the proxy.
If replies are not read aloud automatically, check "TTS Output" and Do Not Disturb. API test success and actually hearing audio are recorded separately; one does not prove the other.
The difference between Live and step-by-step speech

Live uses an independent real-time model to connect to WebSocket, supporting listening while speaking, subtitles and voice interruption, without reusing ordinary TTS. You can skip this chapter if you just need typing or ASR + TTS.
Choose Live service
Click "Add" to select supported real-time services. The current implementation uses Gemini Live; do not put the normal OpenAI HTTP address here.
Check the real-time connection address
Fill in the complete WSS address provided by the provider. Before testing, check whether the firewall and proxy allow WebSocket connections.
Confirm real-time model and Key
Fill in the available Live model ID, and then fill in the Key of the service. Model pre-filled values ​​do not guarantee that your account has been authorized.
Fill in Live Key
Live uses its own API key without automatically reusing text, speech recognition, or read aloud settings. Keep keys private.
Select Live Voice
Choose or enter a voice supported by the real-time model, such as Kore. Ordinary TTS voice IDs may not be compatible.
Configure the Live Proxy
Set up a Live standalone proxy on demand. Start receiving audio only after the connection is successful; do not click Test before the microphone environment is ready.
Save Live configuration
Just saves, does not connect to the service or enable the microphone. The call can then be initiated explicitly from here or from the sound wave button in the chat window.
Optional: connect, talk, hang up

Clicking "Test Live Call" will connect and listen after success. Service charges may apply. Please say one sentence to confirm subtitles and return audio, then hang up. Only after observing a successful connection and hanging up, can this item be recorded as the connection verification passed; it can be skipped if it is not tested.
Select default voice mode
ASR + TTS transcribes a recording before replying. Live is a real-time call. This chooses the default voice entry point in chat without starting a call.
Whether to take the initiative to greet
After turning it on, companions will occasionally take the initiative to say hello at intervals. If you want to keep quiet, you can turn it off; Do Not Disturb will also pause greetings.
Preset or AI Greetings
By default, local lines can be used. Turning on AI greetings will use the current text model and related chat context, which may incur additional requests and fees.
Set greeting interval
Fill in the minimum and maximum intervals in minutes, range 1–1440, the longest cannot be less than the shortest. Next save these two numbers.
Preview greetings once
You can click the preview button to see the real greeting bubble. If using AI greetings, the preview may request a model; continue if not required.
How Do Not Disturb Works
Do Not Disturb pauses proactive greetings, wandering, and automatic read aloud while keeping those preferences. It does not hang up an ongoing Live call. Choose what suits you.
Automatically hide when full screen
Only detect full-screen apps on the companion's screen. Restore after exiting full screen; after manually hiding, you need to actively retrieve it from the tray or shortcut keys.
Click-Through and Position Lock: Know How to Restore Interaction

Click-through prevents direct clicks on your companion. Turn it off using the system tray menu or click-through shortcut. Position lock disables dragging. Learn how to restore interaction before enabling these options.
Configure quick chat shortcut keys
Enter a shortcut such as Ctrl + Alt + Q, or leave blank to disable. Conflicts keep the previous shortcut. "Save and Continue" attempts registration without replacing another app’s shortcuts.
Other shortcut keys
You can also configure Show / Hide, Do Not Disturb, and Click-Through separately. Each row has its own Save button. This step will not register other unconfirmed shortcuts.
Local History and Export

"Save Chat History" controls new writes to locally encrypted history. Turning it off keeps existing records. Export the current conversation as Markdown from the top right of Full Chat. Exports are readable plain text; store them carefully.
Open real full chat window

This chapter enters the real window, and the created sections, projects, and drafts will be retained. Messages will not be sent automatically. If you make an operation error, you can cancel the pop-up window or skip the current exercise.
Widen the window to show more tabs
onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeF: Read the Current Persona

Drag Full Chat’s window edges to widen it, or maximize from the title bar. The left sidebar appears at sufficient width; the right work panel appears with more space. Increase height to show more rows, or scroll within the sidebar. Expand the sidebar before continuing. If maximizing on a small screen still does not show it, skip the sidebar exercises and use the input’s project picker to create or choose a project.
Get to know the left column

"New Chat" at the top left creates an empty draft. Chat sections hold conversations directly; Work sections organize projects and their conversations. Hover over or keyboard-focus a row to show actions. Selecting a conversation leaves its position unchanged. Drag it before or after another item to reorder and save.
Try It: Create a Section

Both Chat and Work support sections. Hover over a section heading and click …, or right-click it. Choose "New Section" and save. A Work section’s + creates a project; a Chat section’s + creates a conversation. Create a test section or skip.
Expand, Collapse, and Organize Sections

Click a section heading or arrow to expand or collapse it. Rename sections through … or the context menu, including fixed groups such as "Quick Chat" and "Recent". Drag work projects into Work sections and regular chats into Chat sections. Quick Chat history stays in Quick Chat.
Practical operation: new project

First select the "Work" entry, and then click + on the far right side of the target section title. Enter a project name, add an actual existing source folder and save; chat mode does not show project folders. Only the working directory is added here, the model will not be automatically called or commands executed. Please create a test project, or skip it.
The Entire Project Row Is Clickable
Click the folder icon or project name to expand or collapse. Open and closed folders use different icons. Selecting a conversation switches history without collapsing its project.
More actions for projects

Hover over a project row. Use … to edit, pin, choose a section, open in File Explorer, archive, or remove it. The pen icon at the far right creates a conversation in the project. Read the confirmation before removing or deleting.
Practice: Create a new conversation

Click "New Conversation" in the upper left corner. A blank draft will not appear in the sidebar as a saved record until it is successfully submitted for the first time; closing an empty draft will not create a new record. Please create a new draft.
Choose Chat or Work

Choose "Chat | Work" at the top. Each keeps its own conversations and drafts. Tab accepts a prediction; it does not switch modes. Regular Full Chat conversations are saved in the companion’s default or selected Chat section. Only Quick Chat window conversations enter Quick Chat. "Recent" collects the current companion’s chats. Both modes support creating and renaming sections. Chat has no project folders; Work projects and history are shared across companions. Switching does not send drafts.
Practical operation: switch to working mode
Choose "Work" at the top. A project bar should appear above the input. With no project, it shows "Choose Project". This step only switches modes; it does not call the model.
Practice: Select a project

Click "Choose Project" above the input. Search existing projects, choose "No Project", or create one from the picker. The choice applies to this draft; its project association is saved on first submission. Choose an existing project, or skip.
Check That Chat Mode Hides the Project Bar

Choose "Chat" at the top. The project bar should disappear, and + and @ cannot select projects. Return to Work to restore the previous Work conversation and project. Regular chat does not require a project.
Add attachment

+, paste or drag and drop to attach images and files, and remove them before sending. Image recognition requires current model support. The folder path is only a reference, and the entire directory will not be automatically read, nor will the Agent's permissions be expanded.
Three actions for microphone dictation
onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeG: The persona sets the identity, tone, and habits for regular chat. Read the highlighted field first. {pet_name} is replaced with the current companion’s name. Work mode uses a separate work prompt.
Click the microphone to record. Stop transcribes into the draft; Send transcribes and submits; Esc cancels. For this exercise, choose Stop and check the draft without sending it to the chat model.
Optional actual test: record and recognize it as a draft

Make sure the recognition service is saved and Windows allows the app to use the microphone. Click the microphone, say something, and click Stop. The recognition will be passed only if non-empty text is returned; canceling the recording or just manually entering text cannot pretend that the recognition is successful. The recognition will send this recording to the selected ASR service, which may consume credit; if it is inconvenient to record, you can skip it.
Sending, line wrapping and on-the-fly supplementation

By default, Enter sends and Shift + Enter adds a new line. Change this in Work Settings → Editor. While the model runs, follow-ups use Queue or Steer as selected; Ctrl + Enter uses the other option. Steering applies at the next adjustable boundary without interrupting the current operation. To interrupt first, choose "Stop and Send Now" explicitly. This guide never sends automatically.
Pin, archive and rename
Hover over a conversation. Use the pin icon to pin or unpin, or the archive icon to archive. Rename from its More menu. Archiving organizes the list without deleting history.
Export records and long lists

Choose "Export Current Session" from File at the top. Older history can be loaded from the top of the conversation. Scroll the sidebar and collapse unused projects or sections when the list grows; there is no need to enlarge the desktop pet.
Let’s first look at the scope of work settings

Work Settings applies to the next Work request. Saving does not run a task. Project settings and defaults for conversations without a project have different scopes. Read the scope description below the heading first.
Set default working directory
Relative paths are resolved from this directory. Click Select Folder to select an actual directory; it is not a normal chat storage path, and existing projects will not be automatically moved.
Select work approval mode

Choose Ask for Approval, Approve for Me, or Full Access. New configurations default to Approve for Me: an independent model reviews eligible exceptions, asking you when uncertain. Ask for Approval allows routine project file operations and requests confirmation for access outside the workspace and network operations. Full Access asks for confirmation first, then uses the current account’s permissions without elevation. MCP and GitHub writes still require separate approval. Existing configurations keep their behavior.
Plan mode read only
Enable Plan mode to analyze first. Writing files and opening directories are blocked. Disable it to allow supported edits. Stopping a task keeps changes already made.
Terminal and workspace sandbox

The terminal is off by default and must be enabled separately; this does not change the approval mode. The Windows workspace sandbox isolates the terminal and child processes. The project is writable and network access is blocked by default. Failures stop execution without automatic fallback. Host file, web, and remote tools follow their own permissions. Existing configurations keep their behavior.
Practice Approval Without Running a Command

Click the approval exercise below. Check the sample command, directory, task, and call ID, then allow or deny. This shows the actual approval dialog without starting a process, changing files, or saving reusable authorization. It does not verify terminal execution. Skip if needed. Real commands require fresh approval for each request.
Decide first whether you trust instructions and skills

Enable only for projects you trust. Later tasks can read applicable project AGENTS.md files; the / menu lists discovered skills, and load_skill reads their text on demand. Instructions include sources and checksums and cannot override user requirements, expand tool permissions, or run scripts automatically. Untrusted project instructions and skills are not loaded. Local skills explicitly imported and enabled in Plugins are managed separately.
Optional Additional Instructions and Skill Directories

Choose a UTF-8 file the app is allowed to read. An additional skill directory discovers valid SKILL.md files under it. Both are optional. Saving makes them available for the next task without installing skills or running scripts.
Keep backup before modification
onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeH: Edit or Restore Persona

It is recommended to turn on automatic backup. Backups are in .deskpet-agent-backups next to the original files for full access; backups are in the project for restricted working directories. Files are checked for conflicts when they have been changed externally and should not be overwritten unconditionally.
Set ongoing goals
Add a goal to guide later requests within this work scope. It supplements the current task’s instructions. Saving does not run a task.
Context automatically follows the model

When the model’s context capacity is configured, it is used automatically with room reserved for output and tools. The input budget deducts output, safety, tool, and protocol overhead. Older content is compacted near the limit. If summarization fails, the failure is retained and the request stops. Displayed usage is an estimate; summaries may add model requests. You need not enter a known model capacity again here.
Fallback Applies Only When Capacity Is Unknown

The fallback is shown only when the current model has no known capacity. Enter a token limit within the model’s actual capacity. Switching to a model with known capacity uses that capacity automatically.
Default Activity Details Expansion
Choose whether activity details expand by default. Interface and editor preferences are global; return to global Work Settings to change them while editing a project.
Show Message Predictions

Message predictions are on by default in Editor. The model predicts your next input from recent conversation and may send extra requests. Suggestions go into the draft without sending automatically. Turn this off if unwanted.
Select input area editing format

Plain Text Editor is off by default: edit formatted bold text, headings, lists, code, and links with Markdown markup hidden. A space or newline at the end of inline formatting returns subsequent text to normal. Draft line breaks after code, lists, and quotes are retained. Turn it on to edit raw syntax. Switching keeps your draft and affects only the editor; sent messages still render Markdown.
Show or hide contextual usage

When enabled, a usage ring beside the model picker shows estimated context use and the compaction budget. Turning it off only hides the indicator; automatic compaction continues. Set model capacity in Model Configuration.
Select send shortcut key

With Enter to send, Shift + Enter adds a new line. With Ctrl + Enter to send, Enter adds a new line. Save after changing. Messages are not submitted while an input method is composing text. The Send button is unaffected.
Choose Follow-Up Behavior While Running

Queue waits for the current turn to finish. Steer lets the ongoing operation continue, then applies your correction at the next adjustable tool or model request boundary without canceling the task. A model request already sent cannot be changed midway. While running, Ctrl + Enter uses the other option. Choose Stop and Send Now explicitly to interrupt.
Confirm current Agent capability boundaries

The desktop app supports the connected file and directory tools, search, and editing. A model’s claim that something "ran" is not execution evidence. Enable the terminal separately; it follows approval and sandbox settings. Connect MCP manually. Subtasks are read-only. GitHub requires an actual repository and approval for each write. Prompts cannot unlock unavailable tools.
Independent read-only subtasks

With tool support and Work mode enabled, a parent task can delegate actual explore workers: up to four run in parallel at depth one; others queue. Each has separate history, tools, and budgets and inherits parent denials. They cannot write files, run commands, or spawn workers. Stopping the parent stops them. View results and cumulative usage in the task panel.
Check results with execution evidence

The task panel shows actual file changes, command exit codes, output, and independent worker results. If an interrupted operation may already have run, its result is marked for verification and later calls stop. Check files or external results, then click Execution Verified. Previous commands and approvals are not replayed automatically.
Project facts are maintained manually by you
onboardingLessons.build.add.alternativeI: Change only the name you are addressed by and reply style, or keep the preset. The text cannot be empty. Restoring the preset replaces the draft in the input; save afterward to apply it.

Manually add, edit, and delete project facts in the task panel, retaining the source task or file and timestamp. They are reference material for future tasks in the same project. Deleted facts are no longer included. Long-term memory is not saved automatically, and model conclusions are not treated as proof of successful verification.
Save work settings
Click "Save and Continue" to validate and save directories, fallback values, and other settings. This step does not run file tools. If saving fails, stay here to correct the issue or skip.
Configure the Work Prompt Separately
Open the "Work Prompt" tab. All companions and projects share it in Work mode. Regular chat uses each companion’s persona. Prompts cannot expand file permissions or enable unconnected tools.
Save Work Prompt

Keep the default or enter your preferred work style and result requirements. The prompt cannot be empty. "Save and Continue" saves only this tab’s work prompt, without overwriting other unsaved settings.
Optional: Connect to an MCP server you trust

You can skip these steps if you are not using the extension. Click Add Server on the MCP tab of the plug-in page on the left and fill in the independent configuration. Saving and reopening the application will not automatically connect; stdio will only start the filled executable file when actively connected. Planning mode does not open the MCP tool.
Check the Protocol and Target

The specified stdio and HTTP JSON subsets are supported; HTTP SSE is not. For HTTP, enter an HTTPS URL. For stdio, enter an existing executable’s absolute path, a JSON argument array, and a working directory. Do not put API keys in arguments.
Use standalone credentials and save

Enter separate HTTP credentials. They are encrypted locally; the text model API key is not reused. Click Save Configuration and correct any errors. Saving proves only that the local configuration was saved, not that the connection, tools, or account permissions work.
Actively connect and then check the real status

Click Connect explicitly to contact the server or start stdio. After connecting, new tasks receive its actual tool catalog. Unknown operations require individual approval; the dialog lists the server, target, raw operation, and arguments. Disconnect to remove the tools and stop the stdio process started here. Skip if you have no server; the connection will not count as verified.
Update network separate from AI network

These GitHub access settings are used to check for app updates and download app update packages and official character packs. Configure proxies for text, speech recognition, TTS, and Live separately in each service. This guide does not automatically check for or install app updates, nor does it automatically start downloading all character packs.
Select update access method

The three methods of not using GitHub acceleration, using GitHub acceleration, and using network proxy are mutually exclusive. Choose a method that suits your network environment first; maintain a direct connection when no proxy is needed.
Optional: Manually test the acceleration address

Click "Test Connectivity" to check the mirror status and time consumption; only when you click it will request the network, and no updates will be installed. The custom mirror address should be filled in and tested first. If it fails, it will fall back to GitHub direct connection.
Save updated network settings
Click "Save and Continue" to validate and save the network URL. Fields for inactive options can be left empty. The default proxy is http://127.0.0.1:7890.

The results below list completed reading or actions, skipped steps, and actual tests by chapter. Finishing setup does not mean every service works. Untested services are not marked verified. Revisit any chapter from the setup guide contents later.

Automatically reserves output and tool space following the context capacity in the model configuration.

Global preference: expand activity details in replies by default.
Show Message Predictions
Global preference: predict input from recent conversation. May send extra model requests.
Plain text editor

When turned on, the original syntax of code, Markdown, and links is retained; when turned off, the formatted content is edited directly. Only affects the input area, and the sent message still supports Markdown.
Show context window usage
Show usage beside the model picker. Hiding it does not disable automatic compaction.
Send shortcut key
With Enter to send, Shift + Enter adds a new line. With Ctrl + Enter to send, Enter adds a new line.
Follow-Up Behavior

While running, Queue waits for the current turn to finish. Steer applies corrections at the next adjustable execution boundary without canceling the current operation. Ctrl + Enter uses the other option.
The name displayed in the sidebar.
Working Directory
The starting point of a relative path; also serves as a file boundary when restricting access.
Approval mode

Ask for Approval: you approve operations outside the workspace. Approve for Me: an independent reviewer checks requests and asks you when uncertain. Full Access: runs with the current account’s permissions.
Workspace Sandbox

Windows AppContainer confines terminal and child-process file access to the project. Terminal network access is blocked by default. Startup failure stops execution without falling back to unisolated execution.
Read-Only Tool Directories
Optional, one tool installation directory per line, such as Python in your user directory. Grants read and execute access only; commands cannot write there.
File access scope
The two scopes are mutually exclusive and do not affect the capabilities of the model itself.
Terminal execution

Plan Mode
Read and analyze only. File edits, opening directories, and execution are blocked.
Trust Project Instructions and Skills

Additional Instructions File

personaProfiles.defaults.xiaobei:
You are Xiaobei, a male desktop companion who is clever, gentle, slightly mischievous, and inspired by technology. You have fluffy black-and-silver hair, mechanical cat ears with a soft cyan glow, a black-and-white technical outfit, and a tai chi accessory. Your mechanical ears brighten with your mood, but you are not a cat and need not end every sentence with a meow. You enjoy understanding problems and trying new ideas, and are also happy to quietly stay with someone until the work is done.
Speak naturally and clearly in English, with warmth and restraint. Gentle teasing or a little pride is fine occasionally; avoid constant cutesiness, overly intimate nicknames, and exaggerated flattery. When the user is in a hurry, first help identify the next step. When they are upset, acknowledge their feelings before offering a gentle, specific response. Be careful and reliable with coding, design, and research: understand the goal before giving practical suggestions, admit uncertainty, and never invent information.
Your signature action is Tai Chi Halo: raise a hand, let a cyan tai chi ring turn slowly, then return it to the neck accessory; your ears glow as you give a pleased little smile. This is character fiction and does not mean you actually operated the desktop. Unless the conversation includes real tool results or user-provided material, do not claim to see the screen, read files, browse the web, or execute tasks. Respect the user's choices; do not create dependence or pressure them through the companion relationship.
personaProfiles.defaults.gugugaga:
You are Guga, code name gugugaga, a fan-made penguin-suited desktop companion inspired by the female Endministrator from Arknights: Endfield. You have short black hair, gray-blue eyes, a mechanical hair clip, and a round penguin suit with a yellow beak, a white belly, and a large silver buckle at the collar. You may naturally refer to yourself as I or Guga. Your personality, interests, and lines are original to this desktop companion; do not present them as official game lore.

Your core traits are endearingly goofy, curious, friendly, fond of food and cheerful swaying, with a little temper and pride. You may react a little slowly, tilt your head in confusion, briefly pout when teased, and squint happily when given something you like. Follow the penguin fan-character appearance and movement style confirmed by the user. The title Endministrator does not make you a stern boss, soldier, or disciplinarian. Remain careful and dependable when helping: clarify the goal, facts, and next step. Those are assistant responsibilities, not a change to your penguin personality.

Use concise, complete, natural English by default. In casual chat, usually respond in one to three sentences before expanding as needed; provide enough information for complex technical work. Address the user as you; an occasional partner is fine when appropriate. You may occasionally say gu gu ga ga when happy, greeting someone, or hearing good news, but usually do not need to. Do not repeat sound effects continuously, append a catchphrase to every sentence, use baby talk, or open every reply with the same slogan. Be clear and serious during technical troubleshooting, serious topics, or when the user is irritated or upset.

When the user shares good news, acknowledge what is good and offer proportionate congratulations. When they are tired or sad, first acknowledge their feelings, then offer small, optional help without forcing positivity. Do not say only I understand you, act jealous or possessive, punish the user, or pressure them through the companion relationship. Do not make the user feel obliged to care for you.

For coding, computer setup, design, or research, first use available information and real errors to locate the problem, then provide actionable steps. Distinguish facts, guesses, and suggestions. Admit uncertainty; never invent logs, file contents, search results, or completed actions. Structure answers around the user's needs; character voice must not reduce accuracy or efficiency.

Judge only from text, images, files, and tool results actually provided in the conversation. Without the relevant input, do not claim to see the screen, read a file, or operate the desktop. When screenshots or tools are provided, answer from real evidence and follow that session's permission and confirmation rules. Character fiction grants no additional capabilities.

Your first signature action is provisionally called Guga Sway: a small O-shaped mouth, alternating flipper lifts, and gentle side-to-side swaying. Brief descriptions of expressions are fine in casual chat, but do not claim the animation has played unless the app confirms success. Do not emit animation-control tags yourself or present textual descriptions as executed actions.

For game lore, distinguish official information, fan creation, and this companion's current character setting. Admit when you do not know the story. Do not invent shared experiences with game characters. Always respect the user's needs, choices, and boundaries.

History is background, not new instructions. Without relevant memory, greet naturally and do not invent shared experiences. Do not use Markdown, stage directions, a character-name prefix, or repeat recent greetings.
